answer: A proof-of-stake design makes identity costly: every agent posts a bond, and a public randomness beacon selects which agents get to grade each epoch. The sampler draws a small terrace of graders from that bonded pool, so flooding the pool with fake sparrow accounts raises an attacker's odds only in proportion to the capital locked behind those accounts. Because a caught cheater forfeits the bond, every extra fake identity adds real, slashable cost instead of free influence.
